Title: Agent vs. Agent: Automated Data Generation and Red-Teaming for Custom Agentic Workflows
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) deployed as autonomous agents with tool access present unique safety challenges that extend beyond standalone model vulnerabilities. Existing red-teaming frameworks like Agent Harm use static prompts and hardcoded toolsets, limiting their applicability to custom production systems. We introduce a dual-component automated red-teaming framework: Agent Harm-Gen generates adversarial tasks and evaluation functions tailored to arbitrary toolsets, while Red-Agent-Reflect employs iterative prompt refinement with self-reflection to develop progressively more effective attacks.Evaluating across 115 harmful tasks (71 generated, 44 from Agent Harm) spanning 8 risk categories, our method achieves substantial improvements: up to 162% increase in attack success rate on o4-mini and 86% success on Gemini 2.5 Pro.Successful attacks systematically decompose adversarial objectives into benign-appearing sub-tasks that circumvent safety alignment, highlighting the need for agent-specific guardrails.
Major_Contribution_Result: The paper proposes AgentHarm-Gen to synthesize adversarial tasks/graders for arbitrary toolsets and Red-Agent-Reflect for iterative self-reflective attack refinement. Across 115 harmful tasks (71 generated, 44 from AgentHarm) in 8 risk categories, they report large gains over static baselines, including up to a 162% increase in attack success/harm score on o4-mini and strong success on Gemini 2.5 Pro; successful jailbreaks often decompose harm into benign-looking sub-tasks.
Research_Limitations_Challenges: The framework inherits AgentHarm's English-only constraint; evaluation focuses on single-turn rather than adaptive multi-turn attacks; automated graders can err; tools are synthetic Inspect-AI tools rather than real-world APIs; and the work does not assess long-horizon planning, self-modification, or sophisticated multi-step attack chains, so results may underestimate real vulnerability scope.
Critics: This is an automated red-teaming/data-generation system for custom agent workflows, not a defense or standardized security gate. Reported relative gains (e.g., 162%) are versus AgentHarm-style baselines under the authors' harm-score protocol and should not be compared naively to unrelated ASR definitions. Reflection prompts for Red-Agent-Reflect are withheld, limiting independent reproduction of the full attack loop.
